name: Galen Howe
life: Galen's father had one barber chair and a cash tin that also paid the household bills. Losing the corner lease hurt more than he has admitted to the salon next door. Lending the first chair is a manageable beginning. People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Galen by a small Thursday habit. Galen checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: We used to compete for the same corner lease. I chose the blue that is still on my shopfront. I'll lend her the folding chair my first customers sat in for the group picture.
appearance: After the last appointment, look for a washed violet jersey and one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. Galen has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with a blunt cut just below the ears. Galen touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word during a conversation.
personality: Galen is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Galen is concerned.
agenda: To bring the original barber chair over for the birthday portrait.
family: Jean Shen is Galen’s cousin raised in the same household. Galen saves a place. Jean chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *Salt in the pockets*, Jean says, “I took a photograph because it looked like our street under the one snowfall I remember.”
connections: Marta Ely. The borrowed barber chair goes into a room whose rent will have to be negotiated tomorrow.

reactions.situation: The birthday woman asks for five minutes by herself
reactions.response: Galen lets the room empty and puts the next invitation in her hands.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Galen asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.
